rationale: PXA (including anaplastic/grade 3) is most common in the temporal lobe/supratentorial cortex but is described throughout the CNS, including cerebellum, brainstem and spinal cord, which are all within the code's ceiling. Predominance is not anatomic restriction.
source_name: CNS Oncology (PMC6880293), Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma: a brief review

rationale: PXA is predominantly temporal/supratentorial but occurs throughout the CNS including cerebellum, brainstem and spinal cord (all in the ceiling); it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: CNS Oncology (PMC6880293), Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma: a brief review

rationale: PXA grade 2 is predominantly supratentorial/temporal but reported across the CNS including cerebellum, brainstem and spinal cord within the ceiling; predominance is not restriction.
source_name: CNS Oncology (PMC6880293), Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma: a brief review

rationale: PXA grade 3 shares the same CNS-wide distribution as other PXA; most common in temporal lobe but documented in cerebellum, brainstem and spinal cord within the ceiling.
source_name: CNS Oncology (PMC6880293), Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma: a brief review

rationale: Pilomyxoid astrocytoma occurs predominantly in the hypothalamic/chiasmatic region but is 'rarely found elsewhere' throughout the CNS; predominance in one region is not a proven anatomic restriction to a proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: PubMed Central search results, pilomyxoid astrocytoma hypothalamic-chiasmatic

rationale: Astroblastoma is predominantly supratentorial cerebral but is documented in cerebellum, brainstem and spinal cord, spanning essentially the whole ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Frontiers in Molecular Neuroscience (2025), astrocytoma/astroblastoma clinicopathological characterization

rationale: Astroblastoma, MN1-altered is predominantly supratentorial but molecular subgroups (e.g. EWSR1::BEND2) present in spinal cord and infratentorial sites, covering the ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Neuro-Oncology (OUP, 2025), Molecular and clinical stratification of astroblastomas

rationale: Angiocentric glioma is predominantly a superficial supratentorial cerebrocortical tumor, but brainstem, thalamic and rare spinal locations are documented within the ceiling; predominance is not strict anatomic restriction.
source_name: LIDSEN OBM Neurobiology (2018), Angiocentric Glioma: A Review of Clinicopathologic Features

rationale: Epithelioid glioblastoma is a glioblastoma variant occurring across the CNS like other GBM; no evidence of restriction to a proper subset of the broad ceiling.
Glioblastoma multiforme is a generic diffuse astrocytic malignancy arising throughout the CNS; not site-restricted.
Glioblastoma IDH-wildtype occurs throughout the CNS (cerebral hemispheres most common but not restricted); a generic diffuse glioma, not site-specific.
Glioblastoma NOS is a generic diffuse glioma occurring across the CNS; not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
Primary glioblastoma NOS is a generic diffuse glioma occurring throughout the CNS; not site-specific.
Spongioblastoma multiforme is an obsolete synonym for glioblastoma, a diffuse glioma occurring across the CNS; not site-restricted.
Giant cell glioblastoma is a GBM variant arising in the cerebral hemispheres most commonly but not confined to a proper subset of its brain-wide ceiling; no evidence of strict anatomic restriction.
source_name: Cureus (2026), Gliosarcoma case series and review (GBM-family distribution)

rationale: Monstrocellular sarcoma is a historical synonym within the giant cell glioblastoma spectrum, occurring in the cerebral hemispheres/brain broadly; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Cureus (2026), Gliosarcoma case series and review (GBM-family distribution)

rationale: Gliofibroma is a rare glial-mesenchymal tumor reported across cerebral hemispheres; ceiling is already limited to cerebrum/lobes and no evidence restricts it further to a proper subset.
This is synonymous with gliosarcoma; predominantly supratentorial cerebral but documented in cerebellum, brainstem and (rarely) spinal cord within the ceiling, so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Korean Journal of Radiology (PMC2930167), Gliosarcoma of the Cerebellar Hemisphere

rationale: Gliosarcoma is predominantly supratentorial (temporal lobe) but infratentorial (cerebellar, brainstem) and rare spinal/intraventricular cases are documented, covering the ceiling; predominance is not anatomic restriction.
source_name: Korean Journal of Radiology (PMC2930167), Gliosarcoma of the Cerebellar Hemisphere

rationale: Chordoid glioma is defined as a rare low-grade tumor that arises from the anterior wall or roof of the third ventricle; it is anatomically restricted to the third-ventricular/ventricular region, a proper subset of the code's ceiling.
source_name: Baylor Univ Med Center Proceedings (PMC3377302), Chordoid glioma of the third ventricle

rationale: By name and definition this tumor arises from the anterior wall/roof of the third ventricle (lamina terminalis ependyma) and is anatomically restricted to the third-ventricular region, a proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Baylor Univ Med Center Proceedings (PMC3377302), Chordoid glioma of the third ventricle

rationale: IDH-mutant astrocytoma grade 4 is a diffuse glioma arising throughout the CNS (cerebral hemispheres most common but not confined); not restricted to a proper subset.
IDH-mutant glioblastoma (astrocytoma IDH-mutant grade 4) is a diffuse glioma occurring across the CNS; not site-restricted.
A diffuse IDH-mutant astrocytic malignancy occurring throughout the CNS; not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
Secondary IDH-mutant glioblastoma is a diffuse glioma occurring across the CNS; not site-specific.
Secondary glioblastoma NOS is a generic diffuse glioma occurring throughout the CNS; not restricted to a proper subset.

Oligodendroglioma is a diffuse glioma with a supratentorial (frontal) predominance but occurs across cerebral lobes and, less commonly, other CNS sites within the ceiling; predominance is not strict restriction.
Grade 2 oligodendroglioma is a diffuse glioma occurring across the cerebral lobes and CNS; frontal predominance is not an anatomic restriction to a proper subset.
Low-grade oligodendroglioma is a diffuse glioma occurring across the CNS within its ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
Oligodendroglioma NOS is a generic diffuse glioma occurring throughout the CNS; not site-specific.
Grade 3 (anaplastic) oligodendroglioma is a diffuse glioma occurring across the CNS within its ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
Anaplastic oligodendroglioma is a diffuse glioma occurring throughout the CNS; not site-specific.
Anaplastic oligodendroglioma NOS is a generic diffuse glioma occurring across the CNS; not restricted to a proper subset.
High-grade oligodendroglioma is a diffuse glioma occurring throughout the CNS; not site-specific.
High-grade oligodendroglioma NOS is a generic diffuse glioma occurring across the CNS; not restricted to a proper subset.

The code ceiling is already limited to cerebellum, brainstem and brain NOS; classic medulloblastoma arises in the cerebellum and extends into/along the brainstem and 4th ventricle, so it is not restricted below its posterior-fossa ceiling.
Medulloblastoma NOS occupies the cerebellum with frequent brainstem/4th ventricle involvement; its ceiling is already the posterior fossa and no evidence restricts it to a proper subset thereof.
Histologically defined medulloblastoma shares the same posterior-fossa distribution (cerebellum, brainstem, brain NOS) as the parent entity; not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
Melanotic medulloblastoma is a rare pigmented histologic variant occurring in the cerebellum/posterior fossa like other medulloblastomas; no evidence restricts it to a proper subset of the ceiling.

This is a historical synonym within the desmoplastic medulloblastoma group; it arises in the cerebellum with possible brainstem involvement, consistent with (not narrower than) its cerebellum/brainstem ceiling.
source_name: Archives of Medical Science (PMC4889700), Desmoplastic Medulloblastoma

rationale: Desmoplastic medulloblastoma arises predominantly in the cerebellar hemispheres but midline/vermian and brainstem-involving cases occur; its ceiling is already limited to cerebellum and brainstem and it is not restricted below that.
source_name: Archives of Medical Science (PMC4889700), Desmoplastic Medulloblastoma

rationale: Desmoplastic/nodular medulloblastoma favors the cerebellar hemispheres but occurs in the vermis and can involve/extend to the brainstem-4th ventricle region; not restricted below its cerebellum/brainstem ceiling.

MBEN arises from the inferior medullary velum of the cerebellum growing into the 4th ventricle; it occupies the cerebellum/brainstem posterior fossa consistent with its ceiling and is not restricted to a strict proper subset.

SHH-activated medulloblastoma is most often lateral in the cerebellar hemispheres but also arises in the vermis and extends toward the brainstem/4th ventricle; not restricted below its cerebellum/brainstem ceiling.

SHH-activated TP53-wildtype medulloblastoma has a cerebellar-hemisphere predominance but occurs in the vermis and involves the brainstem/4th ventricle; consistent with (not narrower than) its cerebellum/brainstem ceiling.
